subject: RFP: Pricing Appendix — Tiered Token Bands & Overage Mitigation
messages:

Subject: RFP: Clarification needed on Pricing Appendix (token bands / overages)

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the response to our RFP. Procurement asked that you confirm a few specific items in the Pricing Appendix so we can compare apples-to-apples across vendors. Please see the items below and attach any supporting pricing tables or language you want to include in the commercial appendix.

1) Commit structure: can you confirm whether your commits are monthly, quarterly, or annual? Please show an example for a 12-month commit with 10M monthly tokens.
2) Overage mechanics: how are overage tokens billed (per-token, per-1k, rounding)? Are they billed in the bill cycle following the overage?
3) Discount schedule: what discounting do you apply for multi-year commits, and is there an incentive for prepay?
4) True-up and carry-forward: do unused commit tokens roll forward or expire? Do you offer a true-up credit at year-end?
5) Minimums and termination: what are minimum monthly commitments, and how are early-termination refunds handled?

We have a tight procurement window and would appreciate a consolidated appendix by EOD Friday.

Attached: RFP_Pricing_Appendix.pdf (our template)

Regards,
Asha
Senior Procurement Manager
EnterpriseCo
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: RFP: Clarification needed on Pricing Appendix (token bands / overages)

Hi Asha — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise commercial appendix you can drop into your RFP template; attaching a csv table with example bands for the 10M/month scenario and a short MSA clause draft.

Summary of proposed commercial mechanics (high level):
- Commit cadence: monthly or annual by mutual election. Default: monthly invoiced in arrears for pay-as-you-go; annual prepay available for committed discount. Example (12-month commit at 10M tokens/month): you can structure as 120M tokens/year paid as 12 monthly invoices at our committed rate, or prepay 120M upfront to receive an additional 7.5% prepay discount.
- Token unit and rounding: tokens are billed per 1,000 input+output tokens ("per-KT") with consumption rounded up to the nearest 1 KT. Example: 1,250 tokens => 2 KT billed.
- Overage pricing: overage rate is the committed per-KT rate multiplied by the applicable overage multiplier (table in attachment). For typical midsize commits (>=50M/mo equivalent), overage multiplier is 1.15x; for small commits (<5M/mo) multiplier is 1.35x. Overage is invoiced in the immediately following invoice cycle.
- True-up cadence: annual true-up by contract year. If total actual consumption > committed consumption, customer pays the delta at the overage rate. If actual < committed and no prepay was chosen, unused tokens expire at year-end (do not auto-credit). For annual prepay customers we offer a one-time rollover of up to 10% of unused tokens to the following year.
- Discount schedule: multi-year terms (2-year, 3-year) receive step discounts: 2-year = additional 3.0% off committed rate, 3-year = 6.0% off. Prepay discount stacks with term discount up to a 12% maximum aggregate discount.
- Minimums & Early Termination: Minimum monthly commit: 1M tokens for enterprise agreements. Early termination (customer-initiated) results in pro-rata non-refundable portion of prepay being retained; we offer a 60-day cure window for remediation. Redwood may offer one-time exit credits for documented platform issues resulting in SLA breaches >2 consecutive months (handled case-by-case).
- Audit & pass-through costs: model major version upgrades that materially change unit economics are communicated 90 days in advance; cloud pass-through fees (e.g., private networking) are billed separately with transparent line items.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Table_v1.csv (banded examples), MSA_pricing_clause_draft.docx

If you want, we can convert the above into your exact RFP appendix format and provide sample line-item calculations for three consumption profiles (10M/mo, 50M/mo, 200M/mo). Are you available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the table?

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Fwd: RFP: Pricing Appendix — negotiation posture

Forwarding Asha's ask and your proposed language — small notes on leverage and concessions:

- Keep prepay discount capped and avoid automatic rollover beyond 10% (protects capacity planning).
- Push to invoice monthly even for annual commits (prepay is a separate flow) to reduce credit exposure.
- For overages, prefer per-KT billing with 30-day invoice — it's simple and matches our telemetry.
- Watch the early-termination language: we can offer a limited refund window only for prepay if we cannot meet SLA and don't provide remediation within 30 days; keep it case-by-case, not an automatic clawback.

Suggest we prepare a short appendix and a 30-minute walkthrough deck for Asha. Marcus — can you build three sample scenarios (10M, 50M, 200M) with numbers and cost per API call equivalents?

—Marissa

Attached are three scenario sheets (pasted below as short notes):
- 10M/mo (baseline): Commit rate = $0.80 per KT, Overage multiplier = 1.25x -> overage $1.00 per KT. Annual cost (monthly invoiced): ~$96k/mo effective after standard 7.5% commit discount.
- 50M/mo (mid): Commit rate = $0.60 per KT, Overage multiplier = 1.15x -> overage $0.69 per KT. Annual prepay discount option = additional 5%.
- 200M/mo (enterprise): Commit rate = $0.42 per KT (volume band), Overage multiplier = 1.05x -> overage $0.44 per KT. Suggested SLA rebate cushion for >99.5% uptime.

Notes: rounding to per-KT favors simplification for procurement comparisons. Will upload csv to the shared Drive link and convert to their template tomorrow morning.

-Marcus

Subject: Final commercial appendix & next steps (EC-2026-RFP-1127)

Hi Asha — following internal reviews, attached are the finalized appendix items for your RFP. Key clarifications in this final:

- Billing unit: per 1,000 tokens (KT), rounded up.
- Commit cadence: monthly invoice by default; annual prepay available with specified prepay discount tiers (see table).
- Overage: invoiced in the following invoice period at the overage rate tied to committed band. For your 10M/month example: committed per-KT $0.80; overage for that band = $1.00 per KT (25% premium).
- True-up: annual year-end true-up. Unused tokens expire unless annual prepay with rollover elected (up to 10%).
- Discounts: multi-year and prepay stack per the attached schedule; max aggregate discount cap = 12%.
- Termination: prepay amounts are non-refundable except in documented cases of significant SLA failure; early termination fees limited to remaining 25% of committed value if customer terminates without cause during first 6 months.

Next steps:
1) If this language matches your RFP template, I can insert it directly this afternoon.
2) We can run a short line-item example for your 10M/month usage in a doc (finalized CSV attached).
3) If procurement prefers quarterly true-ups instead of annual, we are open to discuss — that would adjust pricing cadence and slightly increase administrative overhead.

Please advise preferred next action. If easier, click here to schedule a 30-min slot: https://calendly.com/vanessa-redwood/30min (available Fri 10–1 PST).

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
